before: case value followed by when pattern uses the pattern’s === method to decide whether that branch matches.
For this integer example, 1..3 matches 3 while 1...3 does not. An else branch handles remaining inputs.
After a matching branch is selected, Ruby does not automatically execute the following when branch as C-style switch fallthrough.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
value = 3
case value
when 1..3
  puts "inside"
else
  puts "outside"
end
```
Expected output or behavior: inside. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare a literal pattern and a range pattern without treating === as a universal type-check operator. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
